title: Leveraging learning analytics to enhance immersive teacher simulations: Challenges and opportunities
extended_summary:
This chapter examines how learning analytics can be used to enhance immersive teacher simulations, with a particular emphasis on making teachers’ cognitive, behavioral, and perceptual processes visible and actionable. The paper situates this work within teacher education and argues that immersive simulation environments can serve as a testbed for data-informed professional learning, especially when they are combined with analytics dashboards and multimodal feedback.

The chapter’s central contribution is conceptual and methodological rather than an evaluation of a single intervention. It reviews the broader evolution of teacher analytics and then presents TeacherGen@i, a generative AI-enhanced immersive teacher simulation that collects multimodal data including transcribed speech, interaction logs, and gaze information. The simulation is designed so that preservice teachers create and enact lesson scenarios in a web-based VR classroom with AI-driven student agents powered by a large language model.

The empirical portion describes a case study conducted at one university in South Korea with 33 preservice teachers enrolled in a Digital Education course. The authors analyze the recorded simulation sessions using BERT-based classification aligned to Bloom’s taxonomy, lag sequential analysis, and gaze-based visualizations, then use these outputs to inform a prototype dashboard. Across the chapter, the authors conclude that multimodal analytics can surface novice teaching patterns such as reliance on remembering/understanding-level discourse, structured interaction sequences, and selective visual attention, and that dashboards may support reflective practice and lesson redesign.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generative AI-enhanced immersive teacher simulation platform that uses a large language model to generate adaptive student-agent responses in a virtual classroom for teacher practice and analytics.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the TeacherGen@i web-based VR simulation in a university digital education course to let 33 preservice teachers teach AI-driven student agents, generate lesson scenarios, and then review multimodal analytics dashboards.

findings.finding_summary: Across 33 dialogue sessions (n=33 preservice teachers; 1,269 interaction turns), BERT-based coding showed a predominance of Remembering and Understanding questions, indicating mainly lower-order pedagogical discourse. Sequential analysis identified 215 significant behavioral patterns, including structured TT scaffolding chains, SS reasoning sequences, and less frequent but high-impact ST feedback loops, suggesting the simulation elicited both novice-like and more complex dialogic patterns.
findings.measure: BERT-based Bloom's taxonomy coding of verbal discourse; sequential analysis / lag sequential analysis of interaction patterns

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single case study with multimodal analysis of preservice teachers in one course, so the evidence is qualitative/mixed-methods rather than experimental. The paper does not report causal estimates for the AI tool's effects on learning outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The study shows potentially useful analytic and instructional design implications, but no effect sizes are reported for student/teacher outcomes. Impact is therefore suggestive but unclear rather than demonstrated at a measurable level.
